## Ontario Apartment Entry: Practical Tenant Checklist

For a non-emergency repair entry on **2026-06-18**, the safest approach is to confirm the notice in writing, keep the visit time specific, and document everything before and after the entry. If anything feels unclear, treat it as a scheduling/record-keeping issue first.

## What To Do, What To Save, and a Polite Message Draft

### Practical steps
- Ask for **written notice** if you have not already received it.
- Request a **specific entry window** rather than an all-day range.
- Confirm the **reason for entry**, who will attend, and whether anyone else will be present.
- Make sure the apartment is reasonably accessible at the agreed time.
- If you cannot be home, ask how they will enter and who will lock up afterward.
- After the visit, check for any damage, missing items, or unfinished work and note it right away.

### What to document
- Date and time you received the notice.
- The stated reason for entry and the repair details.
- The exact entry date and time window agreed to.
- Names, company names, phone numbers, and email addresses of anyone involved.
- Photos of the unit before and after the repair, especially if anything could be affected.
- Any messages about rescheduling, access instructions, or follow-up work.
- A short note after the visit confirming whether the repair happened as expected.

### Message draft
Hello [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

Thanks for letting me know about the planned repair entry on **June 18, 2026**.

Please send the notice in writing and confirm the **specific time window** for entry, along with the reason for the visit and who will be attending. That will help me plan accordingly.

Please also let me know if you need any access instructions in advance.

Thank you,
[Your Name]
[Unit Number]

## Tenant Record-Keeping for the Repair Visit

| Item | What to capture | Why it helps |
|---|---|---|
| Notice details | Date received, method, stated reason | Confirms what was communicated |
| Entry schedule | Exact date and time window | Reduces confusion about access |
| People involved | Names, company, contact info | Helps if follow-up is needed |
| Before/after photos | Entry area and any affected spots | Useful if damage occurs |
| Post-visit note | What was done, what remains unfinished | Creates a clear record |
| Follow-up messages | Any changes or complaints in writing | Keeps a paper trail |
